title: BPSEC, BPv7, COSE: Bugfix MacOS build
description:
The usage of PRIi64 and PRIu64 may lead to failed builds on MacOS - at
least it did for me.

This patch fixes this.

notes.body:
Maybe there is a better way to solve this!? I updated libs and depends but that did not help on MacOS. Windows never had a problem.

Ideally we need to drop GLib types for C99 types but that is a very extensive and slow change.

Does this mean that `uint64_t` and `guint64` have different sizes on your machine? If so that seems like a GLib misbehavior. Why would they do that?

> Ideally we need to drop GLib types for C99 types but that is a very extensive and slow change.

GLib is working toward making that easier: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/issues/1484

> Does this mean that `uint64_t` and `guint64` have different sizes on your machine?

They're both unsigned long long here on macOS 11.6.

The issue fixed here exactly matches https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/issues/972 from your link.

Could it be related to the new Apple M1 macs?
Please use G_GINT64_MODIFIER instead, as indicated in the doc/READMe.developer file. We should not have let the initial commit being merged with this.

I did a grep on the source code and we have 536 calls to G_GINT64_MODIFIER versus 162 calls to G_GINT64_FORMAT/G_GUINT64_FORMAT. As the use of G_GINT64_MODIFIER is what is recommended in our documentation, that's why suggested its use instead but it seems like G_GINT64_FORMAT/G_GUINT64_FORMAT is already massively used anyway.
So I'm OK with a merge as-is.

This fix isn't complete because everything needs to mesh.
```
proto_item_append_text() -> g_vsnprintf() -> guint64 -> G_GUINT64_FORMAT
wmem_strbuf_printf() -> vnsprintf() -> uint64_t -> PRIu64
```
However it may be good enough. I just find it odd that this is an issue at all using the same type.
I was really puzzled about that issue as well. I was trying to figure out, if there might be a bug in my glib version on MacOS but could not figure it out.
